follow-up time: Study period of approximately 3 years (1 year before, 7 months during, and 1 year after training program)
study type: Prospective cohort study with historical comparison group
outcome: Incidence of obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASI)
finding: A perineal support program significantly reduced the OASI rate, but continuous reinforcement and training are necessary, especially for vacuum deliveries, to maintain its effectiveness.
mod_finding: The OASI rate was significantly lower with the application of perineal support, even after adjusting for other risk factors.
